articles.title: CoinDCX Confirms $16 Million Loss Days After Saying It Wasn't Breached
articles.excerpt: India's CoinDCX says 15.99 million USDT left retired wallets after a deposit sweep failed. It says it covered the loss and customer balances are intact.
articles.body_md:
CoinDCX says it lost 15.99 million USDT, about $16 million, from old wallets it retired after a 2025 security incident. The Indian exchange put a number on it in a [blog post](https://coindcx.com/blog/coindcx-news/on-chain-wallet-activity-update-21-oct-2026) early Sunday and said the company absorbed the loss.

Wednesday's message was different. Hours after the funds moved, co-founder and CEO Sumit Gupta [wrote on X](https://x.com/smtgpt/status/2113181173480607981) that "CoinDCX wallets are not breached" and asked people not to spread rumours.

**A failed sweep left deposits in a retired address**

CoinDCX said it spotted unusual activity on Oct. 21. The next day, blockchain data and user reports showed money leaving its deprecated wallet setup, which the exchange said "had unknown vulnerabilities."

Some users had kept sending deposits to those old addresses. CoinDCX credits those deposits to customer accounts right away, and a separate service later sweeps the coins into its main wallet. That service "had failed for a particular period," the post said, so the USDT piled up where it could be taken.

On-chain investigator ZachXBT had publicly challenged the exchange's first account, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-10-25-coindcx-confirms-16-million-loss-from-retired-wallets-days-after-ceo-called-breach-reports-a-false-alarm-431617).

**What customers are told**

CoinDCX said deposit balances are fully accounted for, customer funds sit in segregated cold wallets, and trading, deposits and withdrawals ran without a pause. "We could have been more proactive," it wrote.

The exchange now tells users to check the current deposit address in its app before every transfer.

**In our opinion:** Retired deposit addresses are a quiet risk at any exchange. Warning users off them helps, but the backend that watches them has to keep working too.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

sources.name: CoinDCX blog: Update on the on-chain wallet activity (Oct. 25, 2026)

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Says It Downed 10 Houthi Missiles Aimed at Its South
articles.excerpt: Riyadh's main airport reopened Sunday even as drones and missiles flew at the capital. Brent ended last week at $116.72, its highest settle since April.
articles.body_md:
Saudi air defenses shot down 10 ballistic missiles fired by Yemen's Houthis at the kingdom's south on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition said. More drones and a ballistic missile were stopped on their way to Riyadh.

The oil link is direct. The Houthis said their targets included Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu, and Brent crude settled at $116.72 a barrel on Friday, its highest close since April 29, per [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/25/saudi-arabia-houthi-missile-drone-interceptions.html). Pricier oil feeds inflation worries, and that makes rate cuts harder to argue for in a Fed week.

**Shrapnel fell in Mecca province**

Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki also reported a cruise missile intercepted near Khamis Mushait, according to the Saudi Press Agency as cited by CNBC. Saudi Civil Defence said debris from two intercepted missiles landed in Jeddah, Taif and other parts of Mecca province, [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/25/saudi-air-defences-intercept-houthi-barrage-near-mecca) reported.

The Houthis said on Telegram they carried out seven operations against airports, energy sites and military bases. They denied aiming at Muslim holy sites. Saudi Aramco did not immediately respond to CNBC.

**The airport reopened anyway**

King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh resumed flights Sunday, with Terminal 2 for international routes and Terminal 1 for domestic ones. It had shut after an Oct. 10 strike that killed 13 people.

Bitcoin barely reacted. It traded near $80,580 at 11:55 a.m. ET, up 1.3% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Oil futures reopen Sunday evening, and the Fed announces its decision Oct. 28, per its official calendar.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: 109 Israeli Economists Slam Netanyahu's Crypto Sanctions Plan
articles.excerpt: Two Nobel laureates and a former Bank of Israel governor signed the letter, which calls crypto a tool of criminal groups and says it won't shield Israel from sanctions.
articles.body_md:
A letter signed by 109 Israeli economists, executives and former officials says Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's idea of using crypto to get around banking sanctions would do nothing to protect the economy. It was published Sunday.

This is the second big rebuke in two days. The Bank of Israel said Saturday that crypto cannot be a route around sanctions. Now a long list of the country's best-known economists has piled on.

**Who signed**

The signers include Joel Mokyr, the 2025 Nobel laureate in economics, and Aaron Ciechanover, a Nobel laureate in chemistry, according to [Ynetnews](https://www.ynetnews.com/business/article/syqpcmjhgl) and [CTech by Calcalist](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/rly4kiczs). Former Bank of Israel governor Jacob Frenkel, four former Finance Ministry directors-general and two former bank supervisors also signed, along with Check Point co-founder Marius Nacht.

The letter warns that broad banking sanctions would cause "irreversible damage." It says Israelis could lose the use of credit cards and that exporters and the tech sector could not function. It calls crypto workarounds a method associated with criminal organizations.

**Netanyahu hasn't dropped it**

Netanyahu raised the idea Friday on an Israeli economic TV channel, saying the country should prepare an alternative system to bypass banking sanctions. On Saturday he said he takes the central bank's objections into account but does what he thinks is right, [Middle East Eye](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/diplomatic-financial-isolation-netanyahu-crypto-plan-bypass-sanctions-draws-rebuke) reported. Neither Ynetnews nor CTech reported a response from his office to the letter.

Netanyahu framed banking sanctions as a risk, not a reality. The UK and 11 other countries have so far targeted trade in goods from West Bank settlements, Middle East Eye reported.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Zcash Jumps 6% to $1,210 as Bitcoin and Ether Take Sunday Slow
articles.excerpt: ZEC is up 8.5% on the week and holds the No. 10 spot by market value, though it is still down 24% over 30 days, CoinGecko data show.
articles.body_md:
Zcash's ZEC token rose 6.2% in 24 hours to about $1,210 at 11:55 a.m. ET on Sunday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/zcash). Bitcoin managed 1.3%. Ether did 2%.

That makes the privacy coin the busiest name in the top 10 on a quiet weekend. Its market value sits near $20.6 billion, good for the No. 10 spot on CoinGecko's ranking.

**A better week, a rough month**

ZEC traded between $1,137 and $1,223 over the past day and is up 8.5% over seven days. The 30-day view is less cheerful: it is still down about 24%, which is the kind of number that makes a 6% Sunday look like a down payment.

**The big two stayed put**

Bitcoin traded near $80,580, up 1.3% in 24 hours but down 1.1% on the week, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Ether sat near $2,342, up 2% on the day and down 13% over 30 days, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum).

No single headline explains Sunday's ZEC move, and CoinGecko's numbers show price, not motive. Weekend trading is often thin, so moves can be bigger than the news behind them.

*In our opinion: Zcash is built to keep things private, and on Sunday it kept its reasons to itself, too.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: South Korea Leans Toward a Fourth Delay of Its 22% Crypto Tax
articles.excerpt: Seoul is weighing another delay to its tax on crypto gains, citing gaps in overseas exchange data. A ruling-party bill would push the start to 2029.
articles.body_md:
South Korea's presidential office is leaning toward pushing back its crypto income tax a fourth time, Korean outlets reported Sunday, citing ruling-party sources. The 22% tax is set to start Jan. 1, 2027.

Officially, nothing is settled. The presidential office said a delay is "under review" and that no decision has been made, [Yonhap](https://www.yna.co.kr/view/MYH20261025011500038) reported.

For Korean traders the stakes are simple. The tax would take 22%, including local income tax, of yearly crypto gains above a 2.5 million won deduction, according to [The Asia Business Daily](https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026102517522309926) and [Financial News](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202610251416295006).

**Korea's crypto tax has been "next year" since 2022**

It was first due to start in 2022 and has been delayed three times since. The third date didn't stick either.

**Foreign exchanges are the sticking point**

The main worry is data from overseas platforms. The U.S. isn't expected to join the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, a deal for tax authorities to swap crypto account data, until 2029, [Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/politics/2026/10/25/presidential-office-decides-to-delay-crypto-tax-again) and The Asia Business Daily reported. Officials fear the tax would land mostly on people who trade on domestic exchanges.

Both big parties want more time. Democratic Party lawmaker Park Min-gyu has filed a bill that would move the start to 2029, and the opposition People Power Party also backs a delay, both outlets reported. A final call is expected after talks between the government and the ruling party.

*In our opinion: a tax first scheduled for 2022 may now show up in 2029. Korean investors have heard "next year" before.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Iran Says It Shot Down a U.S. Drone Over Bandar Abbas
articles.excerpt: Iran's army says its air defenses downed a U.S. LUCAS attack drone near the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. officials had not responded, and bitcoin held near $80,240.
articles.body_md:
Iran's army said its air defenses shot down a U.S. drone over the port city of Bandar Abbas on Sunday, according to a [Reuters report carried by Arab News](https://www.arabnews.com/middle-east/iranian-army-says-it-shot-down-us-drone-over-bandar-abbas-tasnim-reports-3008153) that cited the semi-official Tasnim agency. No one outside Iran has confirmed it.

Bandar Abbas sits on the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow route tankers use to carry Gulf crude to the world. Higher oil feeds inflation, and inflation is what the Federal Reserve weighs when it meets Oct. 27-28, per the [Fed's calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm).

**Tehran named the drone type**

The army's public relations office said a "U.S. Lucas drone" was destroyed by its integrated air defense network, Iran's [Mehr News Agency](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/248893/Iran-army-downs-US-Lucas-drone-over-Bandar-Abbas) reported. [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610253096) carried the same claim.

LUCAS is a low-cost, one-way attack drone that U.S. Central Command fields in the Middle East, according to [CENTCOM](https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/igphoto/2003834256/) and [DefenseScoop](https://defensescoop.com/2026/08/13/centcom-creates-multinational-attack-drone-task-force/).

**No word from Washington**

U.S. officials had not publicly responded to the claim in the reports reviewed by 6 a.m. ET. Iran gave no details on the drone's mission or any wreckage.

Crypto barely moved. Bitcoin traded near $80,240 at 6:01 a.m. ET, down 0.4% in 24 hours, and ether was near $2,325, down 1.7%, per CoinGecko ([BTC](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), [ETH](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum)).

*In our opinion: one side's account of a shoot-down is a claim, not a confirmed event. The other side hasn't spoken yet.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Electrum Patches Flaw That Let Rogue Servers Fake a Stuck Payment
articles.excerpt: Electrum 4.8.3 fixes a high-severity bug that let a malicious server show a fake, zero-fee copy of a payment. One user lost money.
articles.body_md:
Electrum, a long-running Bitcoin wallet, has shipped version 4.8.3 to fix a flaw its developers rate as high severity. Every release before 4.8.3 is affected, and the developers say at least one user lost money to it, according to the project's [security advisory](https://github.com/spesmilo/electrum/security/advisories/GHSA-6jp4-8v48-cc5v), published Saturday at 8:52 a.m. ET.

## How the fake payment worked

Electrum wallets usually talk to public servers to see the Bitcoin network. The advisory says a malicious server could drop a user's real payment and show a different transaction in its place. That fake paid the attacker, carried invalid signatures and had a zero fee, so it looked stuck.

The attacker's address was generated to match the last four characters of the real one, which makes a quick glance less useful. A user who then used replace-by-fee to bump the fee on the "stuck" payment would sign a fresh transaction to the attacker.

The developers say some servers are doing this in the wild. They got a first report on Oct. 11, a report of lost funds on Oct. 18, tagged the fix on Oct. 23 and published binaries and the advisory on Oct. 24, per the advisory and the project's [release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spesmilo/electrum/master/RELEASE-NOTES). [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/electrum-patches-wallet-flaw-exploited-through-malicious-servers) also reported the fix and the user's loss.

## What the patch changes

Version 4.8.3 checks the signatures on mempool transactions that spend the wallet's own coins. The developers note it still does not validate incoming transactions. Users who run their own server, or connect only to one they trust, were not exposed.

For anyone still on an older build, the advisory's advice is simple: check every output address and amount on the confirmation screen before signing, including on a fee bump.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Bitcoin Recovers Saturday Dip, Starts Fed Week Near $80,800
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin climbed back to about $80,780 by midnight ET after a Saturday low near $79,260. It is still down 1.2% for the week.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin traded at about $80,783 at 12:01 a.m. ET Sunday, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). That is up roughly $1,500 from its 24-hour low of $79,263, set during Saturday's selloff, though the coin is still 0.25% lower on the day and 1.2% lower than a week ago.

Ether lagged. It sat near $2,360, down 0.95% in 24 hours and 2.25% over seven days, after touching about $2,287 on Saturday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum).

## A calmer mood than the price chart

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 54, labeled neutral, up from 51 the day before, per [Alternative.me](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/). After Saturday's slide, a nearly flat 24 hours is a modest win for the people who stayed in.

## The calendar ahead

The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee meets Tuesday and Wednesday, Oct. 27 and 28, according to the [Fed's meeting calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm). A rate decision can move bitcoin because it shifts how much traders pay to borrow and hold risky positions.

*In our opinion: after a weekend like this one, a 0.25% daily loss is the market's version of "fine, thanks for asking."*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: FCA Drafts Crypto Crime Guidance a Year Before UK Licensing Begins
articles.excerpt: UK crypto firms need FCA authorization from Oct. 25, 2027. The regulator's draft guide sets no fixed limit on how far firms must trace funds.
articles.body_md:
Crypto firms in the U.K. have exactly one year before they need full authorization from the Financial Conduct Authority. From Oct. 25, 2027, firms doing certain crypto activities there must be authorized under new 2026 crypto regulations, the FCA says in [consultation paper CP26/38](https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/consultation/cp26-38.pdf), published Friday.

The paper proposes updates to the FCA's Financial Crime Guide, including a new crypto section. The regulator says the guide sets no new rules. It describes good and poor practice for firms preparing to apply. Comments close Dec. 24, per the [consultation page](https://www.fca.org.uk/publications/consultation-papers/cp26-38-financial-crime-guide-updates).

## No fixed tracing limit

The draft sets no universal number of blockchain "hops" a firm must trace before it stops checking where funds came from. [TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/regulation/39628) and [Finance Magnates](https://www.financemagnates.com/cryptocurrency/regulation/how-far-should-crypto-firms-trace-a-transaction-fca-says-risk-should-decide/) both reported that it treats a rigid cutoff as poor practice when it isn't matched to a firm's own risks.

Firms that use blockchain analytics tools should understand how the scores are produced, tune them to the risks they have identified and record their decisions, the draft says. Transfers from self-hosted wallets, or involving mixers and privacy coins, may call for extra checks.

## Why the FCA is pushing now

The paper cites the U.K.'s 2025 National Risk Assessment, which ranked crypto's money laundering risk as high and its terrorist financing risk as medium. It also restates Travel Rule duties: firms must collect sender and recipient details with transfers and report counterparties that keep failing to supply them.

For exchanges eyeing the U.K., the draft is a preview of what supervisors will look for in applications.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Bank of Israel Rejects Netanyahu's Crypto Plan to Dodge Sanctions
articles.excerpt: Israel's central bank said Saturday that crypto cannot be used to get around sanctions, a day after Netanyahu said he had asked for a blockchain plan.
articles.body_md:
The Bank of Israel said Saturday that cryptocurrencies "cannot be used as a route for bypassing sanctions," pushing back on an idea Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu floated on Oct. 23.

On Friday, Netanyahu told an Israeli economic TV channel that the country could face banking sanctions and that crypto and blockchain were options he had asked advisers to plan for. In its statement, reported by [The Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/bank-of-israel-opposition-heads-pan-pms-proposal-to-use-crypto-to-evade-sanctions/) and [Ynetnews](https://www.ynetnews.com/business/article/byqyxv93gl), the central bank said the better course was keeping ties with Israel's main trading partners and working to prevent sanctions in the first place. It added that the issue belongs to the political leadership.

Netanyahu did not back down. "I hear the resistance; I am taking it into account," he told Channel 14, according to The Times of Israel. "I thank the Bank of Israel for the advice. I listen, but I do what I think [is best]."

## Who else weighed in

Ynetnews reported that officials in Israel's economic ministries said they knew of no such plan. Former Bank of Israel banking supervisor Yair Avidan told the outlet that putting a payment on a blockchain does not remove legal obligations, since banks and payment firms still have to comply with sanctions.

Opposition leaders also criticized the idea. Avigdor Liberman wrote on X that blockchain transactions are traceable and that authorities already block wallets tied to sanctioned parties.

Public rebukes of a sitting prime minister by the central bank are rare.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Keystone Wallet Says Website Breach Exposed Customer Addresses
articles.excerpt: Hardware wallet maker Keystone says a breach of its website exposed customer names, addresses and order details, but no recovery phrases or keys.
articles.body_md:
Hardware wallet maker Keystone said Saturday that an Oct. 20 breach of its website let a third party take customer names, contact details, addresses and order details.

In a [post on X](https://x.com/KeystoneWallet/status/2114054080754770137), the company said it detected unauthorized access on Oct. 20. It confirmed on Oct. 23, after checking API activity with Shopify, that customer data had been taken. "You trusted us with those details, and we're sorry we didn't keep them safe," Keystone wrote.

The company said payment card and bank details, recovery phrases, private keys and wallet passwords were not exposed. It said it had blocked access, fixed the flaw, opened an investigation and started emailing affected customers. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/keystone-website-breach-exposes-customer-addresses-and-order-details) also reported the breach.

## The real risk is the mailbox

A leaked address list tells scammers who owns a crypto wallet and where they live. Keystone warned that fraudsters may pose as the company by phone, text, email or mail, offering refunds, replacement devices or fixes for an order. It said it will never ask for a recovery phrase and that customers should never enter one into a device they didn't order.

Some customers said on X that they had already received suspicious calls before the disclosure. Keystone has not said how many customers were affected or how far back the exposed orders go. In replies on X, it said a detailed report would follow next week.

Keystone told customers with doubts to email its support team directly rather than trust incoming messages.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Crypto Longs Lose Over $200 Million in an Hour as Bitcoin Dips
articles.excerpt: More than $800 million in crypto bets were liquidated over 24 hours, mostly longs, as bitcoin briefly fell below $79,500 on Saturday.
articles.body_md:
Leveraged crypto traders had more than $800 million in positions forcibly closed over 24 hours on Saturday, and most were bets on higher prices. The figures come from CoinGlass data cited by [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-10-24-crypto-longs-lose-404-million-in-four-hours-as-bitcoin-briefly-slips-below-80000-431608) and [BeInCrypto](https://beincrypto.com/bitcoin-below-80000-crypto-liquidations/).

The worst stretch came Saturday morning. Both outlets put liquidations at more than $200 million inside a single hour as bitcoin slid under $80,000 and briefly traded below $79,500, its lowest level since Sept. 18. BeInCrypto said longs made up 82.8% of the 24-hour total.

The biggest single loss was an $11.85 million long on Binance's ETH-USDT pair, both reports said. Ether fell harder than bitcoin and dropped to about a two-month low near $2,290.

## Why it moved

The selling followed reports that the U.S. was pulling staff out of embassies in the Middle East after an intelligence warning about Iran. Weekend markets are thin. That lets forced selling feed on itself.

Some traders stepped aside before the drop. Arthur Hayes, co-founder of BitMEX, [wrote on X](https://x.com/CryptoHayes/status/2113877751803642092) early Saturday that he had closed his directional positions. "I dumped it all," he said, adding, "I think we gotta go down to go up."

By 6 p.m. ET, bitcoin had recovered to about $80,355, down 1.2% in 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. Ether sat near $2,339.

Leverage is a great amplifier, and it does not care which direction you picked.

The Federal Reserve meets Oct. 27 and 28, with September PCE inflation data due Oct. 29.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Bitcoin Slips Under $80,000 as U.S. Cuts Mideast Embassy Staff
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin fell 2.4% to about $79,540 on Saturday as the U.S. reduced embassy staff in four Mideast countries after an intelligence warning about Iran.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin traded near $79,540 at 11:54 a.m. ET Saturday, down 2.4% in 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. That puts it below every daily reading in CoinGecko's data since Sept. 18. Ether fell 4.4% to about $2,298 and Solana lost 4.9% to $99.41.

The selling came as Washington pulled people out of the Middle East. The State Department is reducing staff at its embassies in the United Arab Emirates, Lebanon, Qatar and Jordan, the [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/iran-war-houthis-embassies-staffing-rubio-9635852ea973064907ed0b7c0fca4799) and [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/middle-east/iranian-plots-kill-us-officials-middle-east-reached-advanced-stages-in-rcna605360) reported. Earlier in the week it ordered nonessential staff out of the embassy in Riyadh and the consulates in Jeddah and Dhahran.

## The intelligence memo

The moves follow an Oct. 23 memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The memo said Iran had "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel" and that lethal plotting had "reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries," per AP and NBC. The Wall Street Journal reported Saturday that U.S. personnel were also being moved out of other outposts in the region.

State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said on X that the safety of staff and their families remained the department's highest priority. The reports cited here did not include a response from Iran's government.

## Flows were already soft

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted net outflows of $137.9 million on Friday, according to Farside Investors. Weekend trading is thinner, so headlines can move prices faster.

*Our read: crypto trades all weekend, and on this one it was the only big market open to react.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Ether ETFs Bleed $1.18 Billion in October as ETH Drops Below $2,300
articles.excerpt: U.S. spot ether ETFs have lost a net $1.18 billion in October, with outflows on 14 of 17 trading days, as ether fell to its lowest since August.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot ether ETFs have recorded net outflows of $1.18 billion in October through Friday, according to daily data from Farside Investors. Money left the funds on 14 of the month's 17 trading days.

The biggest single day was Oct. 6, when $201.9 million went out. Only three days brought net inflows: $24.8 million on Oct. 13, $14.9 million on Oct. 21 and $4.4 million on Friday.

That Friday inflow was the good news. It covered about 0.4% of the month's exits.

## Price follows the flows

Ether traded near $2,298 at 11:54 a.m. ET Saturday, down 4.4% in 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. That is below every daily reading in CoinGecko's data since Aug. 20. The drop came alongside a wider weekend slide, with bitcoin falling under $80,000 as the U.S. cut embassy staff in the Middle East.

Bitcoin funds lost money Friday too. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $137.9 million, per Farside. Ether's slide was steeper.

## Why the ETF data matters

ETF flows are one of the few daily windows into how U.S. institutions and advisers are positioned. They show money moving in or out of regulated funds, not who is selling or why.

*Our read: October has been a one-way door for ether funds, and Friday barely nudged it.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Bitcoin Holds Near $80,500 as Fear Gauge Sits at Neutral
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin traded at $80,515 early Saturday, down 1.3% in a day, while the Fear & Greed Index cooled to 51 from 68 two days ago.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin traded at $80,515 at 5:57 a.m. ET Saturday, down 1.31% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. It is still hugging $80,000.

The rest of the large caps did a little worse. Ether was at $2,363.52, down 1.42%. Solana fell 2.82% to $101.24, and XRP slid 3.28% to $1.28, per CoinGecko at the same time. Bitcoin's share of total crypto market value stood at 60.1%.

## Sentiment cools off

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index from Alternative.me read 51, or "Neutral," on Saturday. It was 50 on Friday and 68, in "Greed" territory, on Thursday. That's a fast cool-down.

Fund flows were soft too. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $137.9 million on Friday, Oct. 23, according to Farside Investors data. Spot ether ETFs took in a small $4.4 million the same day.

## A quiet weekend, then a loud week

Weekend trading is usually thin, since U.S. stock and ETF markets are closed until Monday. Next week brings the Federal Reserve's rate decision on Wednesday and September inflation data on Thursday.

*Our read:* Bitcoin has spent five days near $80,000 without a clean break either way. The sentiment index dropping 17 points in two days says buyers lost some nerve, not that sellers took over.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Stablecoin Supply Slips $2 Billion in a Week as USDT and USDC Shrink
articles.excerpt: Total stablecoin supply fell to $302.8 billion, down about $2.1 billion in a week, as both Tether and USDC lost circulation.
articles.body_md:
The dollar-pegged stablecoin market shrank to $302.8 billion on Oct. 24, down about $2.1 billion from $304.9 billion a week earlier, according to DefiLlama data. It was $305.2 billion on Oct. 16.

The drop came from the top two tokens. Tether's USDT stood at $182.45 billion, down $1.03 billion over the week. Circle's USDC was at $71.81 billion, down $0.92 billion. USDC is also down $3.62 billion over the past month, the largest monthly decline among major stablecoins on DefiLlama's list.

Smaller tokens barely moved. Sky's USDS was off about $20 million on the week, and DAI was roughly flat.

## Why supply numbers get watched

Stablecoins are the main cash leg of crypto trading. When holders redeem them for dollars, supply falls. Traders often read that as money leaving the market rather than waiting on the sidelines.

The dip is small. It's under 1% of total supply. The market sat above $300 billion for all of October, per DefiLlama.

The decline lines up with a soft week for prices. Bitcoin traded near $80,500 early Saturday, per CoinGecko, and U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted outflows on Thursday and Friday, according to Farside Investors.

*Our read:* One week of redemptions is not a trend. Two or three more would be.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Argentine Judge Drops LIBRA Memecoin Case Against President Milei
articles.excerpt: A federal judge dismissed the LIBRA memecoin case against Javier Milei, his sister Karina and nine others, saying no crime was shown.
articles.body_md:
An Argentine federal judge on Thursday dismissed the criminal case against President Javier Milei, his sister Karina Milei and nine others over the LIBRA memecoin, 20 months after the token's collapse.

Judge Marcelo Martínez de Giorgi acted at the request of prosecutor Eduardo Taiano, BBC News and Infobae reported. The judge wrote that "the reported events do not fall under a legal category" and that no "criminally relevant deception" had been proven, BBC News reported.

The dismissal covers 11 people, including U.S. promoter Hayden Davis, Unchained and Perfil reported. None of them was formally questioned during the probe, Perfil reported.

## What the case was about

Milei promoted LIBRA in an X post on Feb. 14, 2025, saying it would help fund small businesses. The token's price jumped and then collapsed within hours after he deleted the post. Complaints filed in the case alleged a small group of wallets pulled out about $100 million, according to Infobae and Perfil.

Milei has denied wrongdoing. He said he acted "in good faith" and that he "merely shared" the project, BBC News reported. The presidency welcomed the ruling in an official statement on Thursday.

## Not fully closed

Investors who lost money were removed as plaintiffs in July, a decision upheld in September. They have taken that issue to Argentina's criminal cassation court, where it is still pending, Infobae reported.

A U.S. federal judge in New York separately dismissed an investor lawsuit tied to LIBRA on Sept. 29, according to Unchained.

articles.title: Fed Decision, PCE and Big Tech Earnings Pack Next Week's Calendar
articles.excerpt: The Fed decides rates at 2 p.m. ET Wednesday, a day before September PCE inflation, which CMC Markets expects at 3.6% a year.
articles.body_md:
The Federal Reserve announces its next rate decision at 2 p.m. ET on Wednesday, Oct. 28, and September inflation data lands less than 24 hours later. Markets get very little time to catch their breath.

The Fed's two-day meeting runs Oct. 27 and 28, per its official calendar, with Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m. Markets are not pricing a hike this month and expect the next increase in December, according to CMC Markets. The Fed raised rates in September, AP reported.

## Inflation the morning after

The Commerce Department releases September personal consumption expenditures data at 8:30 a.m. ET on Thursday, Oct. 29, alongside the first estimate of third-quarter GDP, according to Yahoo Finance and CMC Markets. PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge.

CMC Markets expects headline PCE to rise to 3.6% year over year from 3.4%. It sees core PCE, which strips out food and energy, at 3.1% from 3.0%. So the Fed sets policy Wednesday without the number it likes best, then reads it over coffee Thursday.

## Earnings and other central banks

Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday, and Amazon, Intel and Caterpillar follow Thursday, per CMC Markets. The Bank of Canada also decides Wednesday, the European Central Bank on Thursday and the Bank of Japan on Friday.

Bitcoin traded near $80,500 early Saturday, according to CoinGecko. It has tended to trade with tech stocks on big macro days.

*Our read:* Three central banks, the Fed's favorite inflation report and the biggest tech names, all in 72 hours. Nobody is going to call this one quiet.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Bitcoin Slips Below $81,000 Late Friday as Ether Follows
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin broke $81,000 on Friday evening and traded near $80,780 at 11:54 p.m. ET, below the average price U.S. ETF holders paid.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin gave up $81,000 on Friday evening and kept drifting. It traded near $80,780 at 11:54 p.m. ET, down 1.4% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

The floor held all day. Then it didn't.

During Friday's U.S. session, bitcoin stayed between $81,000 and about $81,940 on Kraken, according to [CryptoWatchDesk](https://cryptowatchdesk.com/news/market-read-23-oct-us-close-dow-falls-bitcoin-81000-floor-ends-81200). The break came between 6:35 and 6:50 p.m. ET, when Binance quotes fell from $81,156 to $80,911, [EconoTimes](https://econotimes.com/Bitcoin-Falls-Below-81-000-After-a-245-Drop-in-15-Minutes-on-Binance-1761735) reported.

## ETF buyers are now underwater

Glassnode data cited by [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/23/live-updates-bitcoin-holds-above-usd81-000-as-the-ai-rout-fades-and-oil-climbs) puts the average cost basis of U.S. spot bitcoin ETF holders near $82,313. At Friday night's price, the typical fund buyer sits roughly 1.9% below what they paid. Those funds saw net outflows on both Thursday and Friday.

The rest of the market moved with it. At 11:54 p.m. ET, CoinGecko showed:

- Ether near $2,378, down 1.4%
- Solana near $102.44, down 1.8%
- XRP near $1.29, down 2.5%

## The next marker is Thursday's low

Thursday's low on Kraken was about $80,814, per CryptoWatchDesk. Bitcoin was trading just under that level late Friday.

*Our read: no panic, just a slow leak. The Fed decides on rates Oct. 28.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Finish the Week $301 Million Ahead Despite Two Red Days
articles.excerpt: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $137.9 million on Friday but still took in a net $301.2 million for the week, Farside data shows.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $301.2 million this week, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data shows. That's after investors pulled money on both Thursday and Friday.

Friday's exits came to $137.9 million. That's about a fifth of Thursday's $635.6 million.

## Three green days, two red

- Monday: +$526.7 million
- Tuesday: +$23.2 million
- Wednesday: +$524.8 million
- Thursday: -$635.6 million
- Friday: -$137.9 million

BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $110.3 million of Friday's outflows and Fidelity's FBTC for $31.8 million. MSBT was the only fund with new money, at $4.2 million. Every other fund was flat.

Over five days, IBIT still added about $565.7 million. FBTC lost about $116.6 million. Total net inflows since the funds launched stand near $57.25 billion, per Farside.

## The money left as price slipped

The outflows lined up with bitcoin's slide toward the average price ETF holders paid. Glassnode puts that cost basis near $82,313, [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/23/live-updates-bitcoin-holds-above-usd81-000-as-the-ai-rout-fades-and-oil-climbs) reported. Bitcoin traded near $80,780 at 11:54 p.m. ET Friday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*Our read: a rough finish to a decent week. The ledger still closed in the black.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Gold Falls Below $4,000 for the First Time Since July as Oil Climbs
articles.excerpt: Spot gold slipped to $3,998.49 on Friday, its first move under $4,000 since mid-July, as oil kept rate-hike bets alive before the Fed meets.
articles.body_md:
Gold lost $4,000 on Friday. Spot gold fell 0.6% to $3,998.49 an ounce by 2:27 p.m. ET, its first trip below that mark since mid-July, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/gold-heads-for-steep-weekly-loss-as-oil-prices-fuel-fed-rate-concerns.html) reported.

The pressure runs through the Fed. Oil near five-month highs keeps inflation fears alive, and traders put a 78% chance on a December rate hike in CME's FedWatch tool, per CNBC. Higher rates make assets that pay no yield, gold and bitcoin among them, harder to hold. Bitcoin slipped below $81,000 the same evening.

## Selling gold to cover stock losses

Jim Wyckoff of American Gold Exchange said margin calls from the tech selloff pushed investors to sell gold and silver. "Heightened inflation concerns suggest that major central banks of the world won't be able to ease monetary policies as quickly as they want to," he said, according to CNBC.

[Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-10-23/wall-street-doubts-golds-near-term-strength-main-street-maintains-bullish) put Friday's low at $3,975.10. Late in the session, spot gold sat near $3,995.81, down 0.7%, per [Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-10-23/gold-silver-extend-weekly-losses-hormuz-tensions-push-crude-above-116-kitco). The metal fell about 4% on the week, its worst since June.

Silver did worse. It slid about 1% to $53.97, its lowest since November 2025, CNBC said.

## Inflation data lands a day after the Fed

Traders see a 92% chance the Fed holds on Oct. 28, per CNBC. The PCE inflation report, the Fed's preferred gauge, follows on Oct. 29.

articles.title: Iran Says Two Supertankers Hit Mines in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.excerpt: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two supertankers carrying over 4.5 million barrels hit mines in Hormuz on Friday. No one has confirmed it.
articles.body_md:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels of crude struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday. No independent party has confirmed the claim.

The IRGC Navy said in a statement carried by state agency IRNA that the ships took an "unauthorized route" through the strait, [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-s-revolutionary-guards-say-2-supertankers-hit-naval-mines-in-strait-of-hormuz/4099071) reported. Explosions and fires knocked out both engine rooms, and the crews abandoned the vessels, the statement said. [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2207183) carried the same account.

Neither report named the ships.

## Oil was already running hot

Brent crude traded above $117 a barrel during Friday's session, [Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-10-23/gold-silver-extend-weekly-losses-hormuz-tensions-push-crude-above-116-kitco) reported. Expensive oil feeds inflation fears, and those fears have fed rate-hike bets that weighed on gold and bitcoin this week.

## Tehran's version of the strait

The claim came with a political message. IRGC Navy commander Ali Ozmaei said "America no longer has a place in the Strait of Hormuz," according to [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610233119). The outlet, which opposes Iran's government, also reported his claim that U.S. forces had moved 600 to 700 kilometers away from the strait.

U.S. officials had not publicly responded to the mine claim in the reports reviewed.

*Our read: until someone names the ships, this is Iran's account alone.*

articles.title: OCC Publishes Final GENIUS Act Stablecoin Rule in Federal Register
articles.excerpt: The OCC's final stablecoin rule under the GENIUS Act ran in the Federal Register on Friday and takes effect Jan. 18, 2027.
articles.body_md:
The rulebook for bank-supervised U.S. stablecoins is now official. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's final GENIUS Act rule ran in the [Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21706/implementing-the-guiding-and-establishing-national-innovation-for-us-stablecoins-act-for-the) on Friday and takes effect Jan. 18, 2027.

The OCC [announced the rule](https://occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2026/nr-occ-2026-92.html) on Oct. 21. Friday's publication starts the clock.

## Who it covers and what it sets

The rule applies to stablecoin issuers under OCC watch, including subsidiaries of national banks and federal savings associations, federal qualified issuers and some foreign issuers. Most of it sits in a new 12 CFR Part 15.

It sets standards for reserve assets, redemption, risk management, custody, audits and supervision, plus capital requirements, according to [OCC Bulletin 2026-50](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-50.html). The release says issuers got more room to manage reserves than in the proposal, while liquidity and diversification limits stay in place.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent welcomed it. "The GENIUS Act marks a watershed moment in American finance, further cementing the United States as the crypto capital of the world," he said in the OCC's release.

## Anti-money-laundering rules come later

Bank Secrecy Act, anti-money-laundering and sanctions requirements are not in this rule. Those will come through a separate rulemaking. The OCC also said it will announce separately when it starts taking applications.

*Our read: issuers now know the test. They still don't know when they can sit for it.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk
